title: Projects
text: Managing a breeding program of Tartary buckwheat. Tartary buckwheat is less studied than common buckwheat, but it has a higher yield due to being self-compatible (i.e., it doesn’t require pollinators to set seed). Due to this high potential, I am working on creating Tartary buckwheat varieties that are suited for New England conditions. So, traits aiming to be maximized are germination under wet environments as well as increased leaf size.

title: Projects
text:
Project 2
Conducting a field agronomy trial evaluating the growth of common and Tartary buckwheat varieties under varying management treatments. Assessing performance as both a cover and food crop.

title: About Tyler
text:
My goal is to become a coder that is 10% as good as Faith.



I graduated from North Carolina State University with a degree in Biology in 2023.



I worked as a research technician for two years in a cotton genetics and breeding laboratory. My work included supporting breeding efforts, conducting field work such as planting and harvesting, and managing plant growth in controlled-environment settings.
Thanks for checking out my web site!
